summary: 1914 Forest Service log cabin lookout on the Colville National Forest; the 1928 pole tower is gone, the cabin was restored in 2009-2010 and NHLR-registered in 1995.

facts.design: 12 by 12 foot hand-hewn log cabin built in 1914
facts.status_note: The 1914 log cabin stands; the 1928 pole tower and cab are gone.

restoration finished in summer 2010; rotted logs and roof replaced

corrections.why: 4.9 m (16 ft) is the 1928 pole tower, which NHLR and WillhiteWeb say is gone. The standing log cabin has no tower height on record.

corrections.current: The tower still stands, but its cab is gone (FFLA).
corrections.proposed: The 1914 log cabin stands; the 1928 pole tower and its cab are gone.
corrections.why: NHLR says the original log cabin remains and the 1928 tower burned; WillhiteWeb says the tower and cab are gone with debris left. The brief's wording says the tower stands, which no source read supports.
The surviving structure is the 1914 log cabin. The NHLR and TrailChick both describe it as a cabin, and the tower it once carried is gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and WillhiteWeb say 1928. FireLookout.com says the 1930s, and TrailChick credits the Civilian Conservation Corps with a 1930s lookout. The story uses 1928, the date two sources share, and notes the disagreement.

NHLR says the tower stayed in service until the mid-1950s and burned in the 1960s. WillhiteWeb says it lasted into the 1960s. TrailChick says both lookouts were decommissioned in the 1970s. No single year is given in the story or the events.
WillhiteWeb says the platform was removed at some point; FireLookout.com ties its removal to the 1928 or 1930s tower; TrailChick says it came off during the 2010 restoration. Not resolved.

notes_for_editor: The brief's status note (tower still stands, cab gone) and its 4.9 m height describe a pole tower that the NHLR and WillhiteWeb say is gone; corrected. The FFLA Washington list page the brief cites (firelookout.org/lookouts/us/wa/) was not read, so the source of the brief's wording is unchecked. The staffing history comes from newspaper items reprinted by WillhiteWeb (1915, 1919) and FireLookout.com's personnel list (1923, 1929); the 1919 item is written in the future tense, so the story says 'set to run' it. The Slagle brothers are undated, so no events entry was made for them. The 1960s burning and 1970s decommissioning are not pinned to exact years, so no event was made for them either. The weebly page's 1913 and 1915 newspaper items were not used. No photos added. Current access into the cabin is not confirmed. Confidence is medium: the cabin's facts agree across sources, but the pole-tower dates conflict.
